findings.title: Severe Class Imbalance Across Accident Severity Classes
findings.description: The dataset displays pronounced class imbalance across 5,976 cleaned records. Minor incidents account for 4,100 (68.6%), Serious incidents account for 1,645 (27.5%), and Fatal-severity crashes represent a critical minority of 231 (3.9% of recorded accidents). Collectively, severe incidents (Serious + Fatal) make up 1,876 (31.4%).

findings.title: Central Market Junction Leads Total Volume; East Lake Road Leads Fatal Crashes
findings.description: Central Market Junction recorded the highest overall accident volume (445 incidents, including 147 severe cases, 33.0% severe incident share). However, East Lake Road exhibited the highest fatal crash count with 24 fatal-severity crashes (7.5% fatal crash share across 320 recorded incidents), followed by Outer Loop - Sector A with 19 fatal crashes (6.9%). Targeted interventions must distinguish high-frequency minor collision sites from high-fatality corridors. (Note: These reflect observed crash counts rather than exposure-adjusted per-km risk).

findings.title: Bimodal Commuter Peaks Drive Volume, but Night Hours Exhibit Highest Fatal Crash Share
findings.description: Accident occurrence peaks sharply during commuter rush hours, led by 18:00 (608 incidents) and 08:00 (547 incidents). Designated peak periods encompass 3,624 accidents (60.6% of total). Conversely, while Night hours (21:00-04:59) represent only 573 incidents (9.6%), they exhibit the highest fatal crash proportion at 4.71% (27 fatal crashes), nearly double the Afternoon fatal share of 2.70%.

findings.title: Adverse Weather (Fog & Light Rain) Substantially Amplifies Severe Outcomes
findings.description: Under Clear conditions, the fatal crash share is 3.18% (25.5% serious). In dense Fog conditions (321 incidents), the fatal crash proportion surges to 8.10% and the combined severe accident share reaches 45.48% (8.1% fatal, 37.4% serious). Light rain conditions also elevated severe incident share to 39.3%, indicating that compromised visibility and slick surfaces significantly increase crash severity.

findings.title: Highway Links and Higher Speed Limits Strongly Associated with Fatal Crashes
findings.description: Highway Links exhibited the highest fatal crash proportion at 6.03% (63 fatal crashes out of 1044 incidents), more than double the proportion on Collector Roads (2.68%). Across all incidents, fatal crashes occurred on road segments with a mean nominal speed limit of 48.4 km/h, compared to 44.3 km/h for minor crashes.
findings.metric_unit: fatal crash share on highway links (%)

findings.title: Motorcyclists Suffer Disproportionate Severity Among Vehicle Categories
findings.description: Incidents involving Motorcycles (1602 incidents) experienced a 5.06% fatal crash proportion and 30.6% serious injury share (35.7% total severe), compared to a 3.48% fatal crash share for passenger cars. Two-wheeler riders remain exceptionally vulnerable to high-impact trauma, requiring dedicated lane separation and protective enforcement.
